Hi Elena / Mark — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

Recap (what we heard)
- Target SLOs: 99th percentile end-to-end response < 300 ms for streaming responses (client-visible token latency) and p50 < 120 ms for non-streaming single-turn requests.
- Sustained throughput: ~500 requests/sec for the primary tenant traffic profile.
- Concurrency: steady-state ~2k concurrent sessions, with burst capability up to ~3k concurrent sessions for short windows (~3–6 minutes).
- Streaming specifics: low initial-first-byte latency is critical (customers render tokens as they arrive). They also want partial-token granularity streaming (chunked).
- Model footprint: customer will use a 13B quantized variant; average prompt + response sequence length ~600 tokens.

Operational asks we discussed
- Warm pools: they asked about warm pool sizing and how long a warm instance takes to be ready for streaming (model load + warmup cost).
- Scale-up time: goal is to keep user-visible degradation below the SLO during a surge — target scale-up from 10% to 100% of surge capacity within 90 seconds if possible.
- Queueing behavior: preference for short-lived backpressure/429 over large request buffering; they'd rather reject than let latency hit 99th percentile.

Proposed experiment / benchmark plan (what Redwood will run)
1) Steady-state throughput run (30 minutes): 500 req/s sustained, measure p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-streaming paths.
2) Burst start test (replay): ramp from 2k -> 3k concurrent over 30s, hold 4 minutes, then drop. Measure scale-up time, queue length, token-level latency spikes, and tail KV-cache warm behavior.
3) Cold-start stress: start new hosts from zero (no warm pool) to observe worst-case model load times and tail latency.
4) Warm-pool sizing sweep: iterate warm pool at 5/10/15/20% of peak concurrency to show marginal improvement in tail latency and scale-up delta.

Data we need from Atlas AI (please confirm and share)
- A short representative traffic trace (sample of request rates and session durations) — helps reproduce concurrency shape.
- Confirmation of exact model variant name + whether they can run a lighter toy model for initial tests.
- Any networking constraints (private VPC + egress rules) that could impact cold-start artifact collection.

Attachments: warm_pool_sizing.xlsx (workbook with runs), latency_targets_v2.pdf (SLO spec), and I recorded the call (call_recording-20270322.mp3).

Next steps / owners
- Elena: confirm you can share a traffic trace and the model artifact or allow a synthetic equivalent (due by Wed 3/24).
- Mark: confirm acceptable failure mode (429 vs queuing) and whether you want graceful degradation pages shown to users.
- Jordan (assigned): draft the test harness and schedule the first run for Thu 3/25 or Fri 3/26.
- Laura (assigned): monitor cost/runbook constraints and capture any gating items for Dedicated capacity.

If that matches your understanding, we’ll schedule the benchmark window and send a pre-run checklist + test endpoints.

Thanks — Vivek

Quick tech plan from my side — high level, then concrete run config.

High-level notes:
- Warm pool behavior: in our runtime we can pre-load quantized weights and keep KV caches cold. That gets the instance into accept-requests state faster (model ready for inference but with cold caches). Full token-level tail improvements come from keeping a small persistent KV-cache shard warm for hottest users.
- Scale signal: we'll use request concurrency + per-worker token-sent rate as the autoscale signal. Thresholds: trigger new instance at 70% of per-GPU concurrency headroom, terminate at <40% sustained. That should keep us ahead of 99th percentile spikes.

Proposed test harness config (for Thu 3/25)
- Model: atlasai/13b-quant (if you can provide); otherwise we’ll run with redwood/13b-quant-sim as proxy.
- Steady-state: 30 min @ 500 req/s, 600-token avg seq length, 2k simulated concurrent sessions.
- Burst: ramp 2k -> 3k concurrent in 30s; hold 4 min; monitor queueing and 99th latency.
- Warm pool sweep: runs at 0%, 10%, 20% warm pool (pre-warmed instances equal to percent of peak concurrency)
- Cold-start: tear down warm pool and spin new hosts; measure model weight load time and first-token latency.

I’ll prepare the harness and post results to the Drive folder. Vivek — can you confirm whether Atlas requires us to run inside their VPC (we can but need temporary credentials)?

-Jordan
